policy_title: Hillsborough Law: Statutory Duty of Candour
stated: Introducing the Hillsborough Law: a statutory duty of candour on police officers and all public officials.

source.quote: Introducing the Hillsborough Law: a statutory duty of candour on police officers and all public officials, as set out in chapter 20.

bearing_set.reason: A statutory duty of candour on police and all public officials directly affects due process, rule of law, and citizens' legal rights — requiring officials to be truthful in legal/investigative proceedings strengthens accountability and access to justice, core O9 indicators.

Requiring candour from police officers and public officials materially affects the integrity of investigations and the justice system — the specific mechanism the Hillsborough context exposed — directly bearing on whether justice works for victims.

membership_note: Two genuine bearings: O5 (justice-system integrity and accountability) and O9 (due process/rule of law). No non-negligible O10 bearing — the duty binds officials in their official capacity, not citizens' speech or liberty. Fiscal and labour-market effects are too minor to reach any threshold.
